---
title: "Research"
---

I develop machine learning methods and intelligent systems for scientific and autonomous decision-making, with interests in generative models, reinforcement learning, foundation models, agents, and ML systems. Computational biology and automated science are the main application areas where I evaluate these ideas.

## Generative and Foundation Models

I design generative models for sequences with controllable properties, including GANs for 5' UTR optimization and transformer-based seq2seq models for protein-conditional RNA design. This work emphasizes reproducible baselines and validation against held-out predictive models.

## Reinforcement Learning and Decision-Making

I apply reinforcement learning to decision problems such as selecting informative gene panels for senescence biomarker discovery. This involves policy optimization, structure-aware rewards, and evaluation under positive-unlabeled settings common in biological data.

## Agentic Systems, Simulation, and Benchmarking

I build agentic systems for autonomous orchestration and fault recovery in programmable cloud laboratories, and develop CloudBench as an open-framework simulator and benchmark generator for studying these systems offline. Related work includes a contributed talk at the AI Scientist Summer Workshop (Microsoft Research, 2026).

## Representation Learning

I develop graph-based protein representations that combine structural subgraph features with evolutionary information, with the goal of representations that are accurate and interpretable on downstream tasks such as pathogenicity prediction.

## ML Systems

I also work on LLM systems topics in coursework, including extending FlashAttention and PagedAttention to MiniTorch. See the [projects](projects.qmd) page for details.

All projects emphasize reproducible code, strong baselines, and clear communication of methods and limitations.
